blocks.en: The Doctrine of Revelation in the Bible
blocks.es_reference: La Doctrina de la Revelación en la Biblia

blocks.en: Introduction
blocks.es_reference: Introducción

blocks.en: Theology is thinking about God. It includes a number of approaches and specializations that contribute to our understanding of the nature of God, human existence, salvation, and morality.
blocks.es_reference: La teología es pensar acerca de Dios. Incluye una serie de enfoques y especializaciones que contribuyen a nuestra comprensión de la naturaleza de Dios, la existencia humana, la salvación y la moralidad.

blocks.en: The main branches of theology include:
blocks.es_reference: Las principales ramas de la teología incluyen:

blocks.en: Systematic Theology — organizing the teachings of Scripture into a coherent system, dealing with Revelation, God, Jesus Christ, the Holy Spirit, the Church, and Eschatology.
blocks.es_reference: Teología Sistemática — organizar las enseñanzas de la Escritura en un sistema coherente, tratando con la Revelación, Dios, Jesucristo, el Espíritu Santo, la Iglesia y la Escatología.

blocks.en: Biblical Theology — tracing theological themes across the books of the Bible, such as the Kingdom, the Fall, Redemption, and the Messiah.
blocks.es_reference: Teología Bíblica — trazar los temas teológicos a través de los libros de la Biblia, como el Reino, la Caída, la Redención y el Mesías.

blocks.en: Historical Theology — studying the development of Christian doctrine through history, including the Trinity, Justification, the Atonement, and other doctrines.
blocks.es_reference: Teología Histórica — estudiar el desarrollo de la doctrina cristiana a través de la historia, incluyendo la Trinidad, la Justificación, la Expiación y otras doctrinas.

blocks.en: Practical Theology — applying theology to preaching, worship, counseling, pastoral care, and Christian living.
blocks.es_reference: Teología Práctica — aplicar la teología a la predicación, la adoración, la consejería, el cuidado pastoral y la vida cristiana.

blocks.en: Liberation Theology — emphasizing justice and the liberation of oppressed and powerless people.
blocks.es_reference: Teología de la Liberación — enfatizar la justicia y la liberación de los pueblos oprimidos y sin poder.

blocks.en: Feminist Theology — reinterpreting theology from a feminist perspective.
blocks.es_reference: Teología Feminista — reinterpretar la teología desde una perspectiva feminista.

blocks.en: Natural Theology — asking what may be known about God through reason and the natural world apart from Scripture.
blocks.es_reference: Teología Natural — preguntar qué se puede conocer de Dios a través de la razón y el mundo natural aparte de la Escritura.

blocks.en: The purpose of theology is not merely academic. It is not simply to collect information or to master religious ideas. Theology is given so that we may know God truly, trust Him fully, and live in obedience to Him faithfully.
blocks.es_reference: El propósito de la teología no es meramente académico. No es simplemente recolectar información o dominar ideas religiosas. La teología se da para que podamos conocer a Dios verdaderamente, confiar en Él plenamente y vivir en obediencia a Él fielmente.

blocks.en: Theology must never remain abstract. It must move from knowledge to transformation. Truth is not given only to inform the mind, but to shape the life.
blocks.es_reference: La teología nunca debe permanecer abstracta. Debe pasar del conocimiento a la transformación. La verdad no se da solo para informar la mente, sino para moldear la vida.

blocks.en: The starting point of all theology is not man's search for God, but God's decision to make Himself known. If God does not reveal Himself, He cannot be known. The finite cannot reach the Infinite. Therefore, if God is to be known, He must speak.
blocks.es_reference: El punto de partida de toda teología no es la búsqueda del hombre por Dios, sino la decisión de Dios de darse a conocer. Si Dios no se revela, no puede ser conocido. Lo finito no puede alcanzar al Infinito. Por lo tanto, si Dios ha de ser conocido, debe hablar.

blocks.en: "Can you search out the deep things of God? Can you find out the limits of the Almighty?" — Job 11:7
blocks.es_reference: "¿Puedes tú buscar las cosas profundas de Dios? ¿Puedes llegar a la perfección del Todopoderoso?" — Job 11:7

blocks.en: Several primary sources of religious belief are often identified:
blocks.es_reference: Varias fuentes primarias de la creencia religiosa son a menudo identificadas:

blocks.en: Tradition — teachings passed through generations.
blocks.es_reference: Tradición — enseñanzas transmitidas a través de las generaciones.

blocks.en: Human Reason — the logical exploration of faith.
blocks.es_reference: Razón Humana — la exploración lógica de la fe.

blocks.en: Existential Encounter — transformative personal experiences. One interesting phenomenon is the large number of Moslems converting after an appearance of Christ to them.
blocks.es_reference: Encuentro Existencial — experiencias personales transformadoras. Un fenómeno interesante es el gran número de musulmanes que se convierten después de una aparición de Cristo a ellos.

blocks.en: The Bible — the foundational source of divine revelation.
blocks.es_reference: La Biblia — la fuente fundamental de la revelación divina.

blocks.en: These all influence religious belief, but for Christian theology the Bible stands as the final written authority.
blocks.es_reference: Todas estas influyen en la creencia religiosa, pero para la teología cristiana la Biblia se mantiene como la autoridad escrita final.

blocks.en: The Word of God
blocks.es_reference: La Palabra de Dios

blocks.en: In the Bible, the revelation of God is called the Word of God.
blocks.es_reference: En la Biblia, la revelación de Dios se llama la Palabra de Dios.

blocks.en: "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God." — John 1:1
blocks.es_reference: "En el principio era el Verbo, y el Verbo era con Dios, y el Verbo era Dios." — Juan 1:1

blocks.en: "And the Word became flesh and dwelt among us." — John 1:14
blocks.es_reference: "Y el Verbo se hizo carne y habitó entre nosotros." — Juan 1:14

blocks.en: A word is both a means of communication and an expression of thought. If we want to know what God is like, we must know His Word, because it expresses His mind.
blocks.es_reference: Una palabra es tanto un medio de comunicación como una expresión del pensamiento. Si queremos saber cómo es Dios, debemos conocer Su Palabra, porque expresa Su mente.

blocks.en: The Word of God is expressed in several ways:
blocks.es_reference: La Palabra de Dios se expresa de varias maneras:

blocks.en: The Living Word — Jesus Christ.
blocks.es_reference: La Palabra Viva — Jesucristo.

blocks.en: The Preached or Prophetic Word — the proclamation of God's truth.
blocks.es_reference: La Palabra Predicada o Profética — la proclamación de la verdad de Dios.

blocks.en: The Natural Word — God's revelation through creation.
blocks.es_reference: La Palabra Natural — la revelación de Dios a través de la creación.

blocks.en: The Written Word — the Bible.
blocks.es_reference: La Palabra Escrita — la Biblia.

blocks.en: The Enacted Word — Baptism and the Lord's Supper.
blocks.es_reference: La Palabra Actuada — el Bautismo y la Cena del Señor.

blocks.en: God does not desire to remain hidden. The better we know Him, the deeper the relationship we may have with Him.
blocks.es_reference: Dios no desea permanecer oculto. Mientras mejor lo conozcamos, más profunda será la relación que podamos tener con Él.

blocks.en: Methods of Revelation
blocks.es_reference: Métodos de Revelación

blocks.en: God has spoken in many ways.
blocks.es_reference: Dios ha hablado de muchas maneras.

blocks.en: Through nature: "Since what may be known about God is plain to them, because God has made it plain to them" (Romans 1:19).
blocks.es_reference: A través de la naturaleza: "Porque lo que de Dios se conoce les es manifiesto, pues Dios se lo manifestó" (Romanos 1:19).

blocks.en: Through prophets: "In the past God spoke to our ancestors through the prophets at many times and in various ways" (Hebrews 1:1).
blocks.es_reference: A través de los profetas: "Dios, habiendo hablado muchas veces y de muchas maneras en otro tiempo a los padres por los profetas" (Hebreos 1:1).

blocks.en: Through His Son: Jesus Christ is the final and most complete revelation of God Himself. If you want to know what God is like, you must look at Jesus.
blocks.es_reference: A través de Su Hijo: Jesucristo es la revelación final y más completa de Dios mismo. Si quieres saber cómo es Dios, debes mirar a Jesús.

blocks.en: "He who has seen Me has seen the Father." — John 14:9
blocks.es_reference: "El que me ha visto a mí, ha visto al Padre." — Juan 14:9

blocks.en: Through Scripture: 2 Timothy 3:16–17 — "All Scripture is God-breathed." 2 Peter 1:21 — "Men were moved by the Holy Spirit." Hebrews 4:12 — "The word of God is living and powerful." Psalm 119:105 — "Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path."
blocks.es_reference: A través de la Escritura: 2 Timoteo 3:16–17 — "Toda la Escritura es inspirada por Dios." 2 Pedro 1:21 — "Los santos hombres de Dios hablaron siendo inspirados por el Espíritu Santo." Hebreos 4:12 — "La palabra de Dios es viva y eficaz." Salmo 119:105 — "Lámpara es a mis pies tu palabra, y lumbrera a mi camino."

blocks.en: Through experience: Romans 2:14–15 teaches that conscience bears witness to the law written on the heart.
blocks.es_reference: A través de la experiencia: Romanos 2:14–15 enseña que la conciencia da testimonio de la ley escrita en el corazón.

blocks.en: These are not competing revelations, but unified expressions of one divine voice.
blocks.es_reference: Estas no son revelaciones que compiten, sino expresiones unificadas de una sola voz divina.

blocks.en: General and Special Revelation
blocks.es_reference: Revelación General y Especial

blocks.en: General revelation is God's self-disclosure through nature, history, and conscience. It is available to all people.
blocks.es_reference: La revelación general es la auto-revelación de Dios a través de la naturaleza, la historia y la conciencia. Está disponible para todas las personas.

blocks.en: It reveals: God exists, God is powerful, man is accountable. It does not save.
blocks.es_reference: Revela: Dios existe, Dios es poderoso, el hombre es responsable. No salva.

blocks.en: Even moral truth appears in limited form through general revelation. What later came to be called the Golden Rule appeared in earlier cultures in negative form: "Do not do to others what you would not want done to you."
blocks.es_reference: Incluso la verdad moral aparece de forma limitada a través de la revelación general. Lo que más tarde se llegó a llamar la Regla de Oro apareció en culturas anteriores en forma negativa: "No hagas a otros lo que no quieres que te hagan a ti."

blocks.en: Christ gave the fuller and positive expression: Matthew 7:12 — "Therefore, whatever you want men to do to you, do also to them."
blocks.es_reference: Cristo dio la expresión más completa y positiva: Mateo 7:12 — "Así que, todas las cosas que queráis que los hombres hagan con vosotros, así también haced vosotros con ellos."

blocks.en: General revelation gives awareness. It does not provide the way of salvation.
blocks.es_reference: La revelación general da conciencia. No proporciona el camino de la salvación.

blocks.en: Because general revelation cannot save, God has given special revelation.
blocks.es_reference: Porque la revelación general no puede salvar, Dios ha dado la revelación especial.

blocks.en: Special Revelation is God's direct, historical, and redemptive disclosure of Himself. It is found in: the history of Israel, the person and work of Jesus Christ, and the Bible.
blocks.es_reference: La Revelación Especial es la revelación directa, histórica y redentora de Dios mismo. Se encuentra en: la historia de Israel, la persona y obra de Jesucristo, y la Biblia.

blocks.en: Special revelation is progressive. It unfolds through history, moving from early glimpses in Genesis to the fullness of truth in Christ and the New Testament.
blocks.es_reference: La revelación especial es progresiva. Se desarrolla a través de la historia, pasando de los primeros vislumbres en Génesis a la plenitud de la verdad en Cristo y el Nuevo Testamento.

blocks.en: Theories of Inspiration
blocks.es_reference: Teorías de la Inspiración

blocks.en: Scripture is God-breathed, carried along by the Holy Spirit, and profitable for doctrine, reproof, correction, and righteousness.
blocks.es_reference: La Escritura es inspirada por Dios, llevada por el Espíritu Santo, y útil para enseñar, redargüir, corregir e instruir en justicia.

blocks.en: "Knowing this first, that no prophecy of Scripture is of any private interpretation, for prophecy never came by the will of man, but holy men of God spoke as they were moved by the Holy Spirit." — 2 Peter 1:20-21
blocks.es_reference: "Entendiendo primero esto, que ninguna profecía de la Escritura es de interpretación privada, porque nunca la profecía fue traída por voluntad humana, sino que los santos hombres de Dios hablaron siendo inspirados por el Espíritu Santo." — 2 Pedro 1:20-21

blocks.en: Dictation Theory — God dictated Scripture word for word.
blocks.es_reference: Teoría del Dictado — Dios dictó la Escritura palabra por palabra.

blocks.en: Natural Theory — the writers were inspired like other literary geniuses.
blocks.es_reference: Teoría Natural — los escritores fueron inspirados como otros genios literarios.

blocks.en: Partial Theory — only certain parts of Scripture are inspired.
blocks.es_reference: Teoría Parcial — solo ciertas partes de la Escritura son inspiradas.

blocks.en: Dynamic Theory — divine guidance worked through human personality and freedom.
blocks.es_reference: Teoría Dinámica — la guía divina obró a través de la personalidad y libertad humanas.

blocks.en: Plenary Inspiration — all parts of Scripture are fully inspired.
blocks.es_reference: Inspiración Plenaria — todas las partes de la Escritura están plenamente inspiradas.

blocks.en: Verbal Inspiration — the very words of Scripture are inspired.
blocks.es_reference: Inspiración Verbal — las palabras mismas de la Escritura son inspiradas.

blocks.en: The process may be debated. The result is clear: Scripture is from God.
blocks.es_reference: El proceso puede ser debatido. El resultado es claro: la Escritura viene de Dios.

blocks.en: 💡 The Hotel Room: A pastor once checked into a hotel at night. Under a dim lamp, the room looked clean. But when sunlight filled the room the next morning, stains, dust, and crumbs became visible. He reflected, "The room didn't change—only the light did." God's holiness reveals what artificial light hides.
blocks.es_reference: 💡 La Habitación del Hotel: Un pastor se hospedó en un hotel por la noche. Bajo una lámpara tenue, la habitación se veía limpia. Pero cuando la luz del sol llenó la habitación al día siguiente, aparecieron manchas, polvo y migas. Reflexionó: "La habitación no cambió—solo cambió la luz." La santidad de Dios revela lo que la luz artificial esconde.

blocks.en: Affirming Absolute Authority
blocks.es_reference: Afirmando la Autoridad Absoluta

blocks.en: When discussing the nature of the Bible, we often encounter terms like "inerrancy" or "infallibility." While these terms have historical value, they are often framed as negatives—stating what the Bible is not (not errant, not fallible). A much more robust and functional term for the believer is Absolute Authority.
blocks.es_reference: Al discutir la naturaleza de la Biblia, a menudo encontramos términos como "inerrancia" o "infalibilidad". Aunque estos términos tienen valor histórico, a menudo se enmarcan como negativos—declarando lo que la Biblia no es (no errante, no falible). Un término mucho más robusto y funcional para el creyente es Autoridad Absoluta.

blocks.en: The term Absolute Authority focuses on a positive affirmation. It affirms what we are as people of faith and what we believe as a community under the Word. It moves the conversation from technical debates about the mechanics of the text to the practical reality of our relationship with God. To say the Bible has absolute authority is to declare that it is the final, supreme standard for all faith and practice.
blocks.es_reference: El término Autoridad Absoluta se enfoca en una afirmación positiva. Afirma lo que somos como pueblo de fe y lo que creemos como comunidad bajo la Palabra. Mueve la conversación de los debates técnicos sobre la mecánica del texto a la realidad práctica de nuestra relación con Dios. Decir que la Biblia tiene autoridad absoluta es declarar que es la norma final y suprema para toda la fe y la práctica.

blocks.en: This is a vital distinction. When we emphasize "not errant," we are often defending a document. When we emphasize "Absolute Authority," we are affirming a lifestyle and a submission to the King. It means the Bible is the benchmark by which all other claims of truth are measured. We do not stand in judgment of the Word; the Word stands in judgment of us. It provides the "Absolute" ground upon which we build our lives, our ministries, and our hope for eternity.
blocks.es_reference: Esta es una distinción vital. Cuando enfatizamos "no errante", a menudo defendemos un documento. Cuando enfatizamos "Autoridad Absoluta", afirmamos un estilo de vida y una sumisión al Rey. Significa que la Biblia es la norma por la cual se miden todas las demás afirmaciones de verdad. No juzgamos la Palabra; la Palabra nos juzga a nosotros. Proporciona el terreno "Absoluto" sobre el cual construimos nuestras vidas, nuestros ministerios y nuestra esperanza para la eternidad.

blocks.en: Transmission, Illumination, and Preservation
blocks.es_reference: Transmisión, Iluminación y Preservación

blocks.en: God revealed, inspired, and preserved His Word. Transmission includes: canonization, manuscript copying, translation, and preservation for every generation.
blocks.es_reference: Dios reveló, inspiró y preservó Su Palabra. La transmisión incluye: canonización, copia de manuscritos, traducción y preservación para cada generación.

blocks.en: The canon includes 39 Old Testament books and 27 New Testament books. The Old Testament was recognized by the Jewish community long before the time of Christ; the later "Council of Jamnia" (c. AD 90), once widely cited as the moment the canon closed, is now understood to be a modern scholarly reconstruction rather than an actual council that decided the canon — the books were already received as Scripture. The New Testament was recognized by the church. Councils confirmed what believers already accepted as inspired; they did not create the canon.
blocks.es_reference: El canon incluye 39 libros del Antiguo Testamento y 27 libros del Nuevo Testamento. El Antiguo Testamento fue reconocido por la comunidad judía mucho antes de Cristo; el llamado "Concilio de Jamnia" (c. 90 d.C.), citado durante mucho tiempo como el momento en que se cerró el canon, hoy se entiende como una reconstrucción académica moderna y no un concilio real que decidiera el canon — los libros ya eran recibidos como Escritura. El Nuevo Testamento fue reconocido por la iglesia. Los concilios confirmaron lo que los creyentes ya aceptaban como inspirado; no crearon el canon.

blocks.en: Through thousands of manuscripts and careful comparison, textual scholars have shown that the Greek New Testament we possess today reflects the original writings with a very high degree of accuracy, and no essential Christian doctrine rests on a disputed textual variant.
blocks.es_reference: A través de miles de manuscritos y una cuidadosa comparación, los eruditos textuales han demostrado que el Nuevo Testamento griego que poseemos hoy refleja los escritos originales con un grado muy alto de precisión, y ninguna doctrina cristiana esencial depende de una variante textual disputada.

blocks.en: Illumination is the ongoing work of the Holy Spirit that enables the believer to understand and apply these truths. Knowledge alone is insufficient; the Spirit must open our eyes to perceive the spiritual significance of the text.
blocks.es_reference: La iluminación es la obra continua del Espíritu Santo que permite al creyente entender y aplicar estas verdades. El conocimiento solo es insuficiente; el Espíritu debe abrir nuestros ojos para percibir el significado espiritual del texto.

blocks.en: "The person without the Spirit does not accept the things that come from the Spirit of God but considers them foolishness, and cannot understand them because they are discerned only through the Spirit." — 1 Corinthians 2:14
blocks.es_reference: "Pero el hombre natural no percibe las cosas que son del Espíritu de Dios, porque para él son locura, y no las puede entender, porque se han de discernir espiritualmente." — 1 Corintios 2:14

blocks.en: Inerrancy does not refer to translations. It refers specifically to the original autographs. Scripture, as originally given, is without error in all that it affirms.
blocks.es_reference: La inerrancia no se refiere a las traducciones. Se refiere específicamente a los autógrafos originales. La Escritura, tal como fue dada originalmente, está sin error en todo lo que afirma.

blocks.en: Practical Insights and Final Summary
blocks.es_reference: Perspectivas Prácticas y Resumen Final

blocks.en: Examples of faith show how Scripture works in real life. Billy Graham struggled with doubts but affirmed Scripture by faith, and that conviction shaped a transformative ministry. Edwin Rushworth, a skeptic, was changed through daily Bible reading and came to accept the truth of Scripture.
blocks.es_reference: Los ejemplos de fe muestran cómo la Escritura obra en la vida real. Billy Graham luchó con dudas pero afirmó la Escritura por fe, y esa convicción dio forma a un ministerio transformador. Edwin Rushworth, un escéptico, fue cambiado a través de la lectura diaria de la Biblia y llegó a aceptar la verdad de la Escritura.

blocks.en: Authority means that God's truth is revealed rather than discovered.
blocks.es_reference: Autoridad significa que la verdad de Dios es revelada en lugar de descubierta.

blocks.en: Inspiration means that God caused Scripture while working through human authors.
blocks.es_reference: Inspiración significa que Dios causó la Escritura mientras obraba a través de autores humanos.

blocks.en: Illumination means that the Holy Spirit helps believers understand the Word.
blocks.es_reference: Iluminación significa que el Espíritu Santo ayuda a los creyentes a entender la Palabra.

blocks.en: Transmission means that God has preserved the Bible through canonization, copying, and translation.
blocks.es_reference: Transmisión significa que Dios ha preservado la Biblia a través de la canonización, la copia y la traducción.

blocks.en: If God has not spoken, nothing can be known. If God has spoken, everything must be understood through that revelation.
blocks.es_reference: Si Dios no ha hablado, nada puede ser conocido. Si Dios ha hablado, todo debe ser entendido a través de esa revelación.

blocks.en: God has revealed Himself in creation, in history, in Scripture, and in His Son. Because He has spoken, He can be known. Because He can be known, He can be trusted. Because He can be trusted, He must be obeyed.
blocks.es_reference: Dios se ha revelado en la creación, en la historia, en la Escritura y en Su Hijo. Porque ha hablado, puede ser conocido. Porque puede ser conocido, puede ser confiado. Porque puede ser confiado, debe ser obedecido.

Jesus Christ is the final and most complete revelation of God: "He who has seen Me has seen the ____" (John 14:9).

sa.prompt: Explain why God's self-disclosure is necessary for true knowledge of Him. Why can we not reach God on our own?
sa.model: The starting point of all theology is not man's search for God but God's decision to make Himself known. The reason is that the finite cannot reach the Infinite; a creature cannot climb up to the Creator by its own effort or cleverness. If God chose to remain hidden, He simply could not be known. Therefore, if God is to be known at all, He must take the initiative and speak. Knowledge of God always begins on His side, not ours, and that is why revelation is the foundation of everything else we believe.

sa.prompt: What does it mean that the Bible is the final written authority, and how does that compare with tradition, reason, and experience?
sa.model: Several sources influence religious belief: tradition, human reason, existential encounter, and the Bible. Each one shapes what people think about God, and the course does not deny that they have real influence. But for Christian theology the Bible stands above them all as the final written authority. Tradition, reason, and experience must all be tested by Scripture, never the other way around. To say the Bible is the final authority means it is the benchmark by which every other claim of truth is measured, and we submit our thinking to it rather than judging it by our own ideas.

sa.prompt: Describe the five forms in which the Word of God is expressed, and what each one means.
sa.model: In the Bible, God's revelation is called the Word of God, and it is expressed in five ways. The Living Word is Jesus Christ Himself, the Word who became flesh. The Preached or Prophetic Word is the proclamation of God's truth. The Natural Word is God's revelation through creation. The Written Word is the Bible. And the Enacted Word is seen in baptism and the Lord's Supper, where the truth is acted out. A word is both a means of communication and an expression of thought, so to know what God is like we must know His Word, because it expresses His mind.

sa.prompt: Explain the difference between General Revelation and Special Revelation. What does each reveal, and what are the limits of General Revelation?
sa.model: General revelation is God's self-disclosure through nature, history, and conscience, and it is available to all people everywhere. It reveals that God exists, that God is powerful, and that man is accountable to Him. What it cannot do is save; it gives awareness but not the way of salvation. Because general revelation cannot save, God gave special revelation, His direct and redemptive disclosure of Himself in the history of Israel, in the person and work of Jesus Christ, and in the Bible. Special revelation is progressive, unfolding through history from early glimpses in Genesis to the fullness of truth in Christ.

sa.prompt: Why is Jesus Christ called the final and most complete revelation of God? What does John 14:9 add to this?
sa.model: God has spoken in many ways, through nature, through the prophets, and through experience, but His Son is the final and most complete revelation of God Himself. If you want to know what God is like, you must look at Jesus. John 14:9 makes this direct and personal: Jesus said, "He who has seen Me has seen the Father." That means the character, heart, and will of the invisible God are made visible in Christ. The prophets spoke God's words, but the Son is God's own self stepped into our world, so He is the clearest revelation we will ever have.

sa.prompt: Compare the Dictation Theory and the Dynamic Theory of inspiration. What does each say about how Scripture was written?
sa.model: The Dictation Theory holds that God dictated Scripture word for word, so the human writers were essentially taking down exactly what they were told. The Dynamic Theory holds instead that divine guidance worked through the human writer's own personality and freedom, so that the result is fully God's Word and yet still reflects the style of the man who wrote it. The course notes that the exact process may be debated among these theories, but the result is clear either way: Scripture is from God. What matters most is not which theory we hold but that we confess Scripture is God-breathed and carried along by the Holy Spirit.

sa.prompt: What is the difference between Plenary Inspiration and Verbal Inspiration?
sa.model: These two terms describe the extent of inspiration from two angles. Plenary Inspiration means that all parts of Scripture are fully inspired, not just the moral teachings or the doctrinal sections, but the whole. Verbal Inspiration means that the very words of Scripture, and not merely the general ideas, are inspired. Taken together they affirm that inspiration reaches both to every part of the Bible and down to its actual words. This guards against the Partial Theory, which says only certain portions are inspired, and against the idea that God gave only loose concepts and left the wording to chance.

sa.prompt: Why does this course prefer the term "Absolute Authority" over "inerrancy" or "infallibility"?
sa.model: Terms like inerrancy and infallibility have historical value, but they are framed as negatives, telling us what the Bible is not: not errant, not fallible. Absolute Authority is preferred because it is a positive affirmation of what we believe and how we live. It moves the conversation away from technical debates about the mechanics of the text and toward the practical reality of submission to God's Word. To say the Bible has absolute authority is to declare that it is the final, supreme standard for all faith and practice. We do not stand in judgment of the Word; the Word stands in judgment of us.

sa.prompt: Explain how Illumination differs from Inspiration. Who works each, and what is accomplished?
sa.model: Inspiration and illumination are both works of the Holy Spirit, but they are not the same. Inspiration was the Spirit's work in causing Scripture to be written: holy men of God spoke as they were moved by the Holy Spirit, so the text itself is God-breathed. Illumination is the Spirit's ongoing work that enables the believer to understand and apply what was written. Knowledge alone is insufficient, because the person without the Spirit cannot grasp the things of God; the Spirit must open our eyes to perceive the spiritual significance of the text. So inspiration gave us the Word once for all, and illumination opens that Word to each reader.

sa.prompt: Summarize the main point of Unit 1. Why does revelation matter for the Christian life?
sa.model: The whole unit turns on one truth: God has spoken. If God had not spoken, nothing could be known of Him; but because He has spoken, everything must be understood in the light of that revelation. God has revealed Himself in creation, in history, in Scripture, and supremely in His Son. The unit ties this into a chain for the Christian life: because He has spoken, He can be known; because He can be known, He can be trusted; and because He can be trusted, He must be obeyed. So revelation is never merely academic. Theology must move from knowledge to transformation, shaping the life and not only informing the mind.
